annotatedSteps.description: Defining speed variable and time expressions
annotatedSteps.studentWork:
Let the speed of the train be x km/h. Reduced speed = (x − 8) km/h.
Time at usual speed = 480/x, time at reduced speed = 480/(x − 8).

annotatedSteps.teacherAnnotation: × Order of terms inverted: time at reduced speed is greater, so it should be 480/(x − 8) − 480/x = 3

annotatedSteps.description: Simplifying the algebraic equation to standard form
annotatedSteps.teacherAnnotation: ½ Correct simplification method from the formed equation, but carries the sign error from step 2

annotatedSteps.description: Factorising and solving the quadratic equation
annotatedSteps.teacherAnnotation: × Inconsistent factorisation: (x − 40)(x + 32) expands to x² − 8x − 1280, not + 1280

annotatedSteps.description: Rejecting negative root and concluding final speed with unit
annotatedSteps.studentWork:
Speed cannot be negative.
∴ Speed of the train = 40 km/h.
annotatedSteps.teacherAnnotation: ✓ Correct context-based rejection of negative root and proper unit given

teacherNote: Marked against: Defining variable and writing expressions for time at normal and reduced speeds (1); Setting up the correct algebraic relation between times: 480/(x − 8) − 480/x = 3 (1); Simplifying to standard quadratic equation: x² − 8x − 1280 = 0 (1.5); Solving the quadratic equation to find roots (1); Rejecting negative root and stating final speed with unit (0.5). Remember that a lower speed means a greater travel time, so 480/(x − 8) must come first in the difference. Additionally, be careful with signs when factorising: (x − 40)(x + 32) gives a constant term of −1280, not +1280.
